content:
Earlier this month, OpenAI launched the first GPT-6 model paired with Astra. GPT-6 has now been expanded with the all-new GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna models.

GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna are now available

According to the release notes for the ChatGPT desktop app, GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna require fewer tokens to run than the equivalent GPT-5.6 version.

GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna are rolling out to Codex and ChatGPT Work, with token pricing lower than their predecessor GPT-5.6. Sol is suited to complex coding and agentic workflows, while Luna is aimed at focused, high-throughput tasks. Both models will be made available progressively to Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise and Edu users. Free and Go users can access Luna via the desktop app. Actual availability depends on the rollout schedule and workspace settings; Enterprise admins will need to enable the new models. Within ChatGPT, both models are offered on Work and Codex, but not on Chat.

Worth noting: there is no GPT-6 Terra model. As expected, OpenAI is set to drop its mid-tier model and keep only three: Terra (small), Sol (large) and Astra (extra-large).

Below is OpenAI's official announcement:

Although the heaviest, most important projects still require Astra's full depth, different jobs have different scales, rhythms and budgets. So we are extending the GPT-6 family with GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna. GPT-6 Astra opened a new generation of intelligence — these two models push the frontier on cost-effectiveness to make those intelligence advantages more widely available. We trained GPT-6 Sol and Luna using an approach similar to that used for GPT-6 Astra, bringing the breakthroughs Astra delivered on professional work, factual accuracy, coding, computer use and alignment to faster, more affordable models.

The company describes the two new models as more capable than the GPT-5.6 version, while also more affordable than Astra (and the GPT-5.6 version it replaced). For instance, the GPT-6 versions of Sol and Luna are priced 50% lower than the GPT-5.6 version.
